=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:40462-40557 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: In `_review_gate_rate_limit_requeue_decide`, conditions 3 and 4 of the `$head_start` filter end the retry window too early: any trusted-login comment with no `gate_retry`/`gate_escalated` marker, and any `github-actions` comment with no gate marker, moves `$head_start` forward, so `$gate_reruns` is undercounted for `head=unknown` episodes.
  WHY: When the requeue-marker writes fail, `$retries` stays at 0, so an unrelated comment between gate markers lowers `$gate_reruns` (minimax's trace: 3 drops to 2). The PR is then re-dispatched past the 3-attempt cap and `ai:needs-human` is never added. The cited line ranges differ by reviewer (gemini/minimax 40555-40557, luna 40470-40472, minimax comment 40462-40465). minimax and luna rated it MAJOR; gemini stated no severity. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash treat this logic as an accepted residual risk from earlier rounds, and glm rates the related issue NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:40462-40473 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comment added in the last run claims the broad `$head_start` window is "safe only because $retries counts every requeue on this head", but that does not hold when a requeue-marker write fails (`marker=write_failed`). In that case `$retries` is 0 and the cap rests only on `$gate_reruns`, which conditions 3 and 4 (lines 40470-40471) reset. The comment's own first paragraph (lines 40455-40459) contradicts its last sentence.
  WHY: The change is comment-only and adds no runtime failure, but a future maintainer who trusts the stated invariant could remove the only remaining cap. Severity NIT as reported.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A review gate that exits on AUTOFIX_GATE_PR_READ_FAILED rc=75 is picked up again by the next scheduled review sweep instead of being treated as handled."
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/ai-review.yml (the consumer scheduled review path), or an equivalent scheduled review-sweep path
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The PR adds review requeue processing only to `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` and leaves `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` unchanged. A scheduled event does not run the review job (line 58 of `review_autofix.yml`), and no scheduled handler reads the new rate-limit marker or dispatches a retry. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dispute this as a gap: issue §18.E says "The implementer names the exact files", the plan grant excludes the review sweep workflow and template, and `run_review_gate_rate_limit_requeue_pass` re-dispatches the review on every scheduled AI Orchestrate Poller tick.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  PROBLEM: The logic that sets `$head_start` is too broad. It ends the window for `head=unknown` gate markers at any github-actions comment that is not a valid gate marker.
  WHY: Legitimate non-gate `github-actions` comments that appear before the correct `head=known` marker end the episode early, so `$gate_reruns` is undercounted. If marker posts fail or are missed, the PR can be re-dispatched beyond the cap without limit.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:40555-40557 (jq filter for `$head_start` in `_review_gate_rate_limit_requeue_decide`); comment at lines 40462-40465 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Conditions 3 and 4 of the `$head_start` filter end the window for `head=unknown` gate markers too broadly. The comment added in the last run claims the window is safe because `$retries` counts every requeue, but that holds only if the requeue-marker writes succeed.
  WHY: If the marker writes fail and a non-marker `github-actions` comment falls between gate markers, `$head_start` moves past an earlier gate marker. Adding one such comment to `test_review_requeue_counts_gate_reruns_without_requeue_markers` drops `$gate_reruns` from 3 to 2 and `$attempts` to 2, so the PR is re-dispatched past the 3-attempt cap and `ai:needs-human` is never added.
  Note: No hardening suggestions. The broad filter came from earlier autofix runs, and the last run only documents it. Earlier editors rated it NIT.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_review_gate_rate_limit_requeue_decide, lines 40470-40472 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `$head_start` filter treats any `$login` comment without a gate-retry or escalation marker, and any `github-actions` comment without a gate marker, as the start of a new retry window. If a requeue-marker write fails, that reset can erase the only remaining attempt count.
  WHY: After a `head=unknown` gate marker, an unrelated comment followed by another gate marker leaves `$gate_reruns` at 0. If the requeue-marker POST also fails, `$retries` stays at 0, so the PR can be re-dispatched instead of escalating at the 3-attempt cap.
